 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Latest news Social Security Some retirees don’t have to wait until 2027 to see their first new COLA-adjusted payment increase
 Some beneficiaries will see their first payments from Social Security with the 2027 COLA applied hitting bank accounts before the New Year is rung in.
 Kevin Dietsch Calum Roche twitter Managing Editor AS USA About the author Sports-lover turned journalist, born and bred in Scotland, with a passion for football (soccer). He’s also a keen follower of NFL, NBA, golf and tennis, among others, and always has an eye on the latest in science, tech and current affairs. As Managing Editor at AS USA, uses background in operations and marketing to drive improvements for reader satisfaction. Update: Nov 8th, 2026 06:46 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Every year in October the Social Security Administration determines the cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) increase for the following year. The 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) was confirmed at 3.6%, up from 2.8% in 2026 . 
 The increase will affect Americans receiving retirement, disability and survivor benefits, as well as Supplemental Security Income (SSI). That translates to approximately $75 extra a month for the average Social Security beneficiary . Modest, yes, but for those living on fixed incomes, it can mean groceries, medication or an extra tank of gas.
 The first payment to reflect this increase correspond to the month of January, but some beneficiaries will be seeing their payments drop before the New Year is rung in. 
 First payments arrive on December 31, 2026
 Because January 1 is a federal holiday , the Social Security Administration (SSA) will issue the first 2027 COLA-adjusted payments for SSI recipients on Thursday, December 31, 2026 .
 Beneficiaries who began receiving Social Security before May 1997, or who receive both Social Security and SSI, will also receive their January Social Security payment on December 31, as January 3 falls on a Sunday.
 After that, payments roll out in three waves according to beneficiaries’ birth dates, a staggered schedule designed to spread payments throughout the month:
 January 13: Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th 
 January 20: Beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th 
 January 27: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st 
 Payments arrive by direct deposit or other approved payment methods, depending on the recipient’s setup.
 Why your deposit might look smaller
 Even with the COLA bump, some retirees may notice less of a gain than expected. Several factors can trim the net amount:
 Higher Medicare Part B premiums , deducted automatically for most enrollees 
 Taxable benefits , depending on combined income 
 Other applicable deductions , which can reduce the amount received 
 Beneficiaries can confirm payment information through the my Social Security portal at ssa.gov/myaccount .
 What the 3.6% increase says about inflation
 The COLA is based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) , measured each third quarter by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This year’s increase reflects continued inflationary pressure and represents the largest adjustment since the 8.7% surge seen in 2023.
 The 3.6% increase is also significantly higher than the 2.8% adjustment for 2026 , providing additional relief for beneficiaries facing rising costs for essentials such as food, housing and healthcare.
 Staying alert to scams
 Each fall, scammers try to exploit COLA season by posing as SSA agents. Remember: you do not need to apply or provide bank details to receive the COLA increase . It is applied automatically. Be wary of unsolicited calls, emails or texts requesting personal information or payment to activate your benefits.
 Legitimate COLA notices are available by mail or through your online account. For reliable updates, use official sources such as ssa.gov/cola or the SSA’s verified social media accounts.
